questions.question: A person supervising the loading of a tank:

options.text: Does not need to be able to move the vehicle.
Does not need to know about the materials being loaded.
Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified person must watch the loading and unloading of a tank. They must stay alert and within 25 feet of the tank. They must also know the hazards of the materials, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: The only way to properly check your tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tires with your hand.

questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only reliable way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: When other vehicles have trouble seeing you at dawn or dusk, you can increase your visibility by:
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, and in snow or rain, turn on your headlights. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: Generally, a shipping paper must list:

options.text: The location of fire departments along the planned route.

questions.explanation: Shippers must list an emergency response telephone number on hazardous materials shipping papers. There are some exceptions to this rule.

questions.question: To help your vehicle be seen by others:

options.text: Headlights should be turned off during the day.
Headlights should be covered with grease.
Headlights should only be used in the rain.

questions.explanation: Clean headlights provide more light at night. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: Placards should be used:

options.text: Any time a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
If there is open space in the truck.
If the amount of hazardous materials in the truck exceeds 200 pounds.
If the hazardous materials create an inhalation hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what class of materials are being carried and warn others of the dangers.

questions.question: A person working on a disabled vehicle on the shoulder of a road:

options.text: Will likely pay attention to traffic on the road.
May be focused on the repair and not paying attention to roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not paying attention to roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on disabled vehicles. They are focused on repairs and may not notice traffic or other hazards.

questions.question: The controlled braking method is:

options.text: When the driver locks the wheels and steers.
When the driver uses the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
When the driver only slightly taps the brakes.
When the driver downshifts the gears to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the driver uses the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. If you need to steer while braking, release the brakes, steer, then brake again.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, so it looks like a wet road.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is involved in a crash on the road ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Block the driver in with your vehicle.
Stop after the crash scene and report the driver's aggressive behavior to the police.
Continue driving and mind your own business.
Pull over and yell at the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop after the crash scene and report the driver's aggressive behavior to the police.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop a safe distance away and wait for police. Tell them about the aggressive behavior you saw.

questions.question: Tank vehicles usually have:
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have high centers of gravity. This makes them tip over more easily. Drive slowly when turning and going around curves.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will:

options.text: Allow you to drive faster than you would be able to otherwise.
Allow you to follow other vehicles more closely than you would be able to otherwise.
Allow you to drive less carefully than you would be able to otherwise.

questions.explanation: ABS helps you keep control during hard braking. It does not make your vehicle stop in a shorter distance.

questions.question: A convex mirror is sometimes called a ____ mirror.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles use curved convex mirrors called "bug-eye" mirrors. These mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tire problem you should check for and avoid?

options.text: Radial and bias-ply tires used together
Recapped tires on the front of a school bus
All tires are made by the same company

questions.correctAnswerText: All tires are made by the same company
questions.explanation: Check tires for: low or high air pressure, excessive wear, cuts or damage, tread separation, dual tires touching each other, mismatched sizes, mixed radial and bias-ply tires, cut or cracked valve stems, and regrooved or recapped tires on school bus front wheels. It is not necessary that all tires come from the same company.

questions.question: Stopping distance can be affected by:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your speed. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop.

questions.question: Placards must be placed:

options.text: In any manner, as long as they are visible.
So words and numbers are read from left to right.
Within three inches of other markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers are read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed so words and numbers read from left to right. Keep them at least three inches away from other markings.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should not:

options.text: Try to get out of their way.

questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Do not provoke them by making eye contact, racing, or refusing to move. Ignore any gestures meant to upset you.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.
To test the lights on the trailer.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) operates the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, remember that:

options.text: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
The package should be placed in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.
The package should be made of wood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation passes through each package and affects nearby packages. The number of radioactive packages you can load together is limited by law.

questions.question: Manhole covers should:
questions.explanation: Keep manhole covers closed and sealed during transit to prevent leaks. Check that the covers have gaskets and close properly.
